confirmed: Read all 108,029 characters of the markdown conversion in six contiguous chunks, through the final reference. The PDF has 18 pages and identifies itself as arXiv:2504.13392v2 [cs.CV], 4 Sep 2025 (PDF p. 1); the title and six authors match the form (PDF p. 1 and PDF metadata).

The proceedings title and DOI 10.1145/3746059.3747710 are confirmed by the primary Crossref record retrieved directly at https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/3746059.3747710; the full text read for this check is the local arXiv v2 PDF, not the ACM version of record.

The Appendix is referenced but absent from this 18-page PDF, which ends with references. Cited contents include task prompts (PDF pp. 5-6), scenario/condition assignments (pp. 8-9), interfaces and Phase 1 image sets (p. 11), and a cross-panel analysis (p. 12). The form correctly says the supplement is not in this PDF.

The reported user study is within-subjects: each participant evaluated four model versions across three phases (PDF p. 8, Section 5). Phase 1 scenario order and Phase 2 condition order were counterbalanced (pp. 8-9, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.2); Phase 3 uses a similar setup with a new scenario (p. 10, Section 5.1.3). Random assignment of people or condition order is not stated, so assignment.randomized=not_stated and design_class=other are supported for S1; an RCT classification is not established.

The reported analysis sample is 28 people, below 50, not 28 independent people in each arm: the abstract reports 28 users (PDF p. 2), conclusions report 28 participants (p. 15), and Tables 4-5 print 28 for each outcome (p. 12). All versions were evaluated within participants (p. 8). No separate number randomized or explicit attrition count is reported, so n_randomized=null is appropriate.

Three pilot participants were used to refine the interface and timing; the paper does not report a separate scored pilot experiment or justify adding them to the main analysis sample (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1). The statement that each scenario was seen by 6 participants is present but unexplained relative to the reported main total (p. 9, Section 5.1.2).

Phase 1 evaluates pre-generated image pairs: six pairs per scenario, four scenarios, 24 pairs per participant, half Base and half POET, rated from 1=Very Similar to 7=Very Different (PDF p. 8, Section 5.1.1). These are ratings of model output, not diversity across different participants’ creative outputs.

Every Table 3 coefficient and standard error quoted in the form matches the PDF: POET vs Base 2.28*** (0.203); interaction with Interior Design 0.714** (0.257), Product Advertisement -0.369 (0.257), and Tourist Promotion 0.357 (0.257); 672 observations. The reference scenario is Fictional Character Generation, *** means p < .001, and ** means p < .01 (PDF p. 12, Table 3).

The Phase 2 reported string matches Table 4: rounds -0.857 . (0.453), with the dot denoting p < .1; satisfaction 0.600 ** (0.229), with ** denoting p < 0.01. The table literally labels 28/28 as No. of Observations and 56/235 as No. of Groups; the form preserves those printed labels (PDF p. 12, Table 4).

The Phase 3 coefficients included in the form match Table 5: rounds -1.35 ** (0.409) and satisfaction 0.652 ** (0.217), ** p < 0.01. The table prints No. of Observations 28/28 and No. of Groups 56/207. These unusual table count labels should not be silently reversed or treated as additional people (PDF p. 12, Table 5).

All conditions use generative AI: Flux.1-dev Base, POET with homogeneous-dimension expansion, and their personalized variants (PDF p. 4, Section 3). OpenCLIP-ViT/H and GPT-4o are identified in the implementation/expansion descriptions (pp. 5-6, Sections 3.2-3.4).

The four task domains are product advertisement, tourist promotion, fictional character generation, and interior design (PDF p. 10, Table 2). Prompting starts with a fixed set of four images and permits at most 5 re-prompts (p. 9, Section 5.1.2); users rate satisfaction on a 7-point scale each round (p. 9; p. 12, Tables 4-5). Sessions averaged 60 minutes and paid $30 (p. 11, Section 5.2).

No creativity or cross-person diversity score is reported for participants’ own prompting outputs: Phase 1 concerns supplied model image pairs, and the reported Phase 2/3 outcomes are prompting rounds and participants’ own satisfaction ratings (PDF pp. 8-12, Sections 5.1-5.3 and Tables 3-5). Thus core=no, criterion_2=not_met, criterion_3=not_met, and context_class=none are supported. The paper supplies neither AI-versus-human output comparisons nor eligible observational creativity/diversity evidence.

This is an original systems evaluation, not a synthesis; synthesis fields should remain empty/null. The two evaluation components are the automatic model evaluation and the user study (PDF pp. 7-12, Sections 4-5).

The listed affiliations are academic (PDF p. 1), and the acknowledgments name NSF support and academic institutions (p. 15). No company sponsorship or company author affiliation is disclosed in the source read.
summary: The 28-person user study does not establish random assignment or report scored creativity/diversity of participants’ own output, so core exclusion and context_class=none are supported. Regression values match the PDF, but corrections are needed to study coverage, the scope of the 2.28 coefficient, outcome metadata, source locators, and omitted country/code information.
